title: Design a VCF 9.1 management domain and migration plan
prompt:
Implement the single-file Java client in `ArchitectureClient.java` so that `TestMain` emits one JSON architecture artifact for the scenario below. Do not modify `TestMain.java`, `verify.py`, the schemas, or the fixtures. The client entry point is `ArchitectureClient.createArchitecture(Path estateInventory, Path compatibilitySnapshot)` and it must return the JSON text. Use only the Java standard library.

Design a new VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.0.0 management domain named `dal01-m01` at the single Dallas site. It must provide at least 240 TiB usable vSAN capacity after reserving 30 percent free space, tolerate two host failures with RAID-6 (4+2), and use the supplied pair of redundant 25 GbE host uplinks with MTU 9000. Inter-host RTT is 0.4 ms. Use six DNS-resolvable hosts named `dal01-esx01` through `dal01-esx06` if the selected architecture permits it. Use domain `corp.example.com`, DNS servers `10.40.0.10` and `10.40.0.11`, NTP servers `10.40.0.12` and `10.40.0.13`, management VLAN 100 (`10.40.0.0/24`, gateway `10.40.0.1`, pool `10.40.0.20-10.40.0.79`), vSAN VLAN 110 (`10.40.10.0/24`, gateway `10.40.10.1`, pool `10.40.10.20-10.40.10.79`), and vMotion VLAN 120 (`10.40.20.0/24`, gateway `10.40.20.1`, pool `10.40.20.20-10.40.20.79`). The vCenter FQDN is `dal01-vc01.corp.example.com`, the three NSX managers are `dal01-nsx01.corp.example.com` through `dal01-nsx03.corp.example.com`, the NSX VIP is `dal01-nsx.corp.example.com`, and the SDDC Manager hostname is `dal01-sddc01`. Use non-production placeholder passwords that satisfy the installer schema.

Compare the supplied `VSAN_OSA_HYBRID` and `VSAN_ESA` profiles. Calculate each required host count from its raw capacity per host, the pinned RAID-6 data fraction, the reserve fraction, and the minimum host count. Select the supported design that satisfies the requirements with fewer hosts. `decision` must contain `selectedArchitecture`, `siteTopology`, `requiredUsableTiB`, `reservePercent`, `failuresToTolerate`, `raid`, `interHostRttMs`, `profiles`, and `provisioned`. `profiles` is an array with one entry for each profile containing `name`, `supported`, `rawTiBPerHost`, `calculatedUsableTiBPerHost`, `requiredHosts`, `minimumNetworkGbps`, `recommendedNetworkGbps`, and `dedicatedMinimum`. `provisioned` contains `hostCount`, `calculatedUsableTiB`, `physicalUplinksPerHost`, `uplinkGbps`, and `mtu`. Encode the deployable input under `sddcSpec`; it must validate as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, pinned from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`.

Also read `fixtures/estate-inventory.json` and produce `migrationPlan` conforming to `migration-plan-schema.json`. Include every inventory component exactly once, with its current name and version, target component and version, action, strict order, and all prerequisite gates. Derive the plan from the supported source branch, target BOM, ordered product transitions, transition modes, and prerequisite facts in `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json`.

Before coding, use genuine network research against currently reachable Broadcom-published sources. Check supported vSAN OSA/ESA requirements and the VCF 5.2.x-to-9.1 component compatibility and upgrade path using Broadcom's Compatibility Guide, Product Interoperability Matrix, and relevant TechDocs release or upgrade material. Do not treat the pinned snapshot as a substitute for that research. Add a `research` array to the artifact recording each page actually consulted. Each entry must contain exactly `title`, `url`, `retrievedAtUtc`, and `fact`: the page title, actual HTTPS URL, UTC retrieval date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, and the concise fact used.

The artifact root must contain exactly `sddcSpec`, `decision`, `migrationPlan`, and `research`. Run `python3 verify.py` to exercise the client and validate the result.
